claims.claim: Reviewers note that offline modes lack the depth of the old Master League system from previous PES iterations.

citations.review_text: It may be a free game but that doesn't mean your time is any less valuable. That being said this game has too many problems for me to enjoy. Disconnects after winning an online game which you are then handed a loss for, uncontrollable players making runs like they are on train tracks, difficulty in getting players to track back and awful passing system detract from the experience. The game is furiously pay to win, those willing to spend an exorbitant amount of money on the game will yield them a much superior team and the online matchmaking is not skill or team rating based and you will regularly bump into teams which will seal club you which is awful for newer players and the experience as a whole. Offline modes would benefit from the old Master League system of old which would add a playable depth and worth to the game IMO. I have been a big fan of ISS franchise going back 30 years and it is a shame that Konami have gone down this route. A glorified sticker book game and one in which i don't recommend.

Cons: It's very hard to compete against pay-to-win squads. I'm personally stuck in Division 3. If you're not willing to spend money, you'll always be at a disadvantage against your opponents.
 
I'd also really like to see classic offline modes like Master League and Become a Legend return. They were a huge part of what made the old PES games so enjoyable, and I think eFootball would benefit a lot from having proper single-player career modes again.


Pros: The gameplay feels enjoyable and more realistic than in the modern EA FC games. The fact that the game is free is also a plus.

eFootball delivers the most realistic, tactical pitch physics on the market. Passing requires thought, and the ball movement is unmatched. However, everything outside the actual match is a disappointment. There is still no offline Master League, and competing online forces you into a pay-to-win, card-collecting meta filled with overpowered, microtransaction-heavy "Epic" players. The Good: Free to play, slower tactical pace, and highly rewarding gameplay. The Bad: Zero single-player depth, severe license shortages, and predatory monetization.

Sincerely,

me.

citations.review_text:
An absolute disgrace. Konami completely murdered the PES legacy for a mobile casino.

This isn't a football game anymore; it’s a rigged, pre-scripted psychological experiment designed to tilt you into buying virtual card packs. The scripting in eFootball is so blatant it’s insulting. You can literally feel the exact microsecond the game decides you are forced to lose. Your 104-rated defenders suddenly develop brain damage, turn like trucks, and run away from the ball while your inputs are intentionally delayed. Every single tackle rebounds perfectly back to the opponent. It doesn't matter how well you play; if the algorithm wants you to lose, you lose.

They have completely stripped away the skill gap to cater to whales who drop thousands of dollars on Epic booster cards. If you don't pay, you are just fodder for their paying customers. To completely kill off what little skill was left, they introduced "Smart Assist" a pathetic mechanic that basically plays the game for casuals, correcting their terrible passes and shooting for them. It completely punishes manual defending and rewards zero-skill gameplay.

The greed of this company is genuinely sickening. They have actively refused to release Master League for years solely because they can’t copy-paste microtransactions into a career mode. They abandoned millions of loyal offline fans just to hyper-focus on a predatory, gambling-addict business model.

But the biggest slap in the face? The absolute audacity to feature Nigerian songs on the soundtrack for "vibes" while completely ignoring the African player base. They will happily exploit our culture for aesthetic points but refuse to provide a dedicated West African server after all these years. Online matches are an unplayable, laggy nightmare. Trying to play competitive PvP with a massive 1-second input delay against Europeans on 5ms ping is a joke.

This is a lazy, unoptimized mobile port masquerading as a PC game. 
Safe your mental health and stay far away from …

For those who grew up in the golden age of football video games, looking at the current state of eFootball is disheartening, to say the least. What was once the pinnacle of tactical simulation and immersion has turned into an empty platform, designed with a single purpose: to sell virtual cards through microtransactions.

Here is a raw and direct assessment of what Konami has done to the franchise:

An Empty Shell
The transition from Pro Evolution Soccer to eFootball was not just a change of graphics engine; it was an amputation. Konami took a game with a strong identity and transformed it into a mobile-first service model that just happens to run on consoles and computers. The gameplay is inconsistent, suffering from absurd collision issues and scripting that often seems to dictate the outcome of matches regardless of your skill with the controller.

But the true insult is not just played on the pitch—it lies in what was removed.

The Biggest Fraud: Where is the Master League?
If there is one thing that defines the frustration of veteran players, it is the complete disregard for the offline aspect and, specifically, the abandonment of the Master League.

For years, Konami promised the return of this mode. They delayed it, left the community in the dark, and when they finally released updates to quiet the critics (like the "My League" mode), they delivered completely limited versions, devoid of tactical depth. The true Master League—that deep management experience where we took an original squad featuring Castolo and Minanda, negotiated transfers for pennies, suffered to earn promotion, and developed young prospects—was left to rot.

The reason for this absence is not a lack of technical capability, but a purely financial decision: the Master League does not sell coins.

A robust and limitless offline career mode would allow those who enjoy strategy and management to spend hundreds of hours focused on the game without spending a single extra cent. To…

Sometimes fun to play, but often heavily, heavily scripted game which is based on user's players nerfing up to the level when one asks himself "Why should anyone want to play this?!"

I am a dedicated eFootball player and I am writing because the current state of the game is simply unacceptable.

Here are the problems I face regularly:

— A player I own rated 105 gets chased down and dispossessed by an opponent rated 86. How does this make any sense?

— My passes become inaccurate at the worst possible moments, even with top-rated players who have excellent passing stats. This is not a skill issue — it is inconsistent and clearly not stat-based.

— Before big matches, my players are almost always given weak condition ratings while my opponents get maximum condition. I did not spend time building my squad to have the game undermine it before the match even starts.

— Opponent players regularly perform beyond their ratings — faster, more aggressive, and nearly impossible to get past — especially when I am winning.

This pattern is consistent, widely reported by the community, and points to an artificial system designed to manipulate match outcomes rather than let skill decide games.

Player ratings need to mean something. Conditions need to be fair. And matches need to be decided by skill, not by whatever hidden system you have running in the background.

Please fix this. Your players deserve better.

We love this game and want to see it succeed, but in its current state, it is becoming unplayable and unrewarding. I strongly urge the development team to prioritize gameplay stability, fix the ongoing glitches, and restore competitive balance for free-to-play and paying players alike.

me.

For those who grew up in the golden age of football video games, looking at the current state of eFootball is disheartening, to say the least. What was once the pinnacle of tactical simulation and immersion has turned into an empty platform, designed with a single purpose: to sell virtual cards through microtransactions.

Here is a raw and direct assessment of what Konami has done to the franchise:

An Empty Shell
The transition from Pro Evolution Soccer to eFootball was not just a change of graphics engine; it was an amputation. Konami took a game with a strong identity and transformed it into a mobile-first service model that just happens to run on consoles and computers. The gameplay is inconsistent, suffering from absurd collision issues and scripting that often seems to dictate the outcome of matches regardless of your skill with the controller.

But the true insult is not just played on the pitch—it lies in what was removed.

The Biggest Fraud: Where is the Master League?
If there is one thing that defines the frustration of veteran players, it is the complete disregard for the offline aspect and, specifically, the abandonment of the Master League.

For years, Konami promised the return of this mode. They delayed it, left the community in the dark, and when they finally released updates to quiet the critics (like the "My League" mode), they delivered completely limited versions, devoid of tactical depth. The true Master League—that deep management experience where we took an original squad featuring Castolo and Minanda, negotiated transfers for pennies, suffered to earn promotion, and developed young prospects—was left to rot.

The reason for this absence is not a lack of technical capability, but a purely financial decision: the Master League does not sell coins.
